llm.summary: The skill is mostly a coherent Gateway restart profiler, but it asks agents to run it with elevated privileges and advertises an elevated Windows script that is not included for review.

dimensions.detail: Restarting Gateway is disclosed and purpose-aligned, but it can interrupt service, and combining that action with elevated execution is broader authority than the artifact justifies.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, package dependency installation, persistence hook, or automatic startup modification was found, but the instructions reference a Windows PowerShell script that is not present in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The agent instructions direct elevated execution for both Linux and Windows, while the reviewed Linux behavior is mostly log parsing, report generation, and Gateway stop/start; no artifact shows why the whole script needs administrator/root authority.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill writes timestamped reports under ~/.openclaw/logs and uses a temporary sort file removed afterward; it does not install services, scheduled tasks, shell hooks, or persistent agent instructions.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The documented purpose is profiling OpenClaw Gateway restart performance, and the Linux script does stop and restart Gateway, parse logs, and generate text/HTML reports, which fits that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a profiler that restarts OpenClaw Gateway and may interrupt active work. Prefer running the Linux script without elevated privileges under the OpenClaw user, and do not rely on the advertised Windows path unless the missing PowerShell script is supplied and reviewed. Treat generated HTML reports as network-dependent because they load Chart.js from a CDN.
llm.findings:
[TP4] expected: The Gateway stop/start behavior is not purpose-mismatched because the skill name, description, and usage text describe restart profiling and explicitly say the agent will stop then start Gateway.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The elevated=true invocation is a material concern: it grants high-impact authority without a clear need or a user confirmation step scoped to the restart action.
[SQP-2] expected: The Linux script's Gateway stop/start is expected for restart profiling, but users should be aware it can cause downtime.
[SQP-2] unexpected: The generated HTML report loads Chart.js from jsDelivr without an integrity attribute, creating an external browser dependency that is not clearly disclosed in the skill instructions.
[SQP-3] expected: The Chinese-only user-visible text is a usability limitation, not a security concern, and the skill metadata and documentation are also written in Chinese.
[T05] unexpected: The static finding is supported in part: the artifact instructs elevated execution for the entire profiler and references an elevated Windows PowerShell path even though only the Linux Bash script is present.
[T08] unexpected: The static finding is supported: the report HTML imports Chart.js from a public CDN at view time without Subresource Integrity, so report rendering depends on unaudited remote JavaScript.
